info.name: HustleHub+ Part 3 - DevSecOps, Monitoring and Finalisation
info.description: Complete regression collection for HustleHub+: the Part 2 auth, gig and booking requests plus Part 3 transactions, income/tax insights, admin RBAC (every admin route checked for 403 as client and freelancer), account lockout, token revocation and security headers. Run against an empty database. In CI it runs through the nginx container: newman run postman/HustleHub_Part3.postman_collection.json --insecure --env-var baseUrl=https://localhost:3000/api --env-var adminEmail=... --env-var adminPassword=...

item.name: Register - A second Freelancer (for ownership tests)

exec: pm.test('Status is 400 - admin role cannot self-register', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test('Generic message, no user enumeration', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Invalid email or password.'));

item.name: Login - Failure (non-existent email, same generic message)

exec: pm.test('Identical generic message to wrong-password case', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Invalid email or password.'));
pm.test('Gig has an id and the submitted title', () => { pm.expect(gig._id || gig.id).to.exist; pm.expect(gig.title).to.eql('Logo design'); });

item.name: Create Gig - Success (second freelancer's own gig, for ownership tests)
Create Gig - Failure (client cannot create a gig - RBAC)
Browse Gigs - Success (public, no auth required)
My Gigs - Success (freelancer sees only their own)

exec: pm.test('Only contains gigs owned by this freelancer', () => { gigs.forEach(g => pm.expect(g.title).to.not.eql('Website copywriting')); });

item.name: Update Gig - Success (owner updates their own gig)
Update Gig - Failure (cannot update another freelancer's gig - ownership)

exec: pm.test('Status is 404 - not found for a non-owner, not 403', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

item.name: Delete Gig - Failure (cannot delete another freelancer's gig - ownership)
Create Booking - Success (client books a gig, simulated payment)

exec: pm.test('Booking is recorded as a paid transaction', () => pm.expect(booking.paymentStatus).to.eql('paid'));

item.name: Create Booking - Failure (freelancer cannot book - RBAC)
Create Booking - Failure (gig does not exist)
My Bookings - Success (client sees their own booking)
Freelancer Bookings - Success (sees bookings against their gig)
Freelancer Bookings - Failure (client cannot access - RBAC)
Freelancer Income - Success (derived from completed transactions)

exec: pm.test('totalIncome matches the booked gig price (300, after the price update)', () => pm.expect(income.totalIncome).to.eql(300));

item.name: Freelancer Income - Failure (client cannot access - RBAC)
Create Booking - Success (returns a separate, linked transaction record)

exec: pm.test('Transaction is linked to the booking (both ways)', () => { pm.expect(transaction.booking).to.eql(booking._id); pm.expect(booking.transaction).to.eql(transaction._id); });
pm.test('Transaction is linked to both users', () => { pm.expect(transaction.client).to.eql(booking.client); pm.expect(transaction.freelancer).to.eql(booking.freelancer); });

item.name: My Transactions - Success (client sees payments made)

exec: pm.test('Every transaction belongs to the client', () => list.forEach(t => pm.expect(t).to.have.property('reference')));

exec: pm.test('Failed login attempts are in the security log', () => pm.expect(logs.map(l => l.event)).to.include('auth.login.failure'));
